note: Pigou price-of-anarchy fixture (#89): a §2-conformant edge_attributes FeatureCollection exhibiting a GENUINE price of anarchy (PoA > 1), which the hand-built toy_network.geojson (PoA ≈ 1) cannot. Topology is the classic Pigou two-link parallel network: a single origin node 0 and destination node 1 joined by TWO one-way directed edges in parallel. Edge 0 (9100001:0:F) is the CHEAP, LOW-CAPACITY link — lower free-flow time (36.0 s) but only 900 vph capacity, so it congests sharply under load. Edge 1 (9100002:0:F) is the near-CONSTANT, HIGH-CAPACITY link — higher free-flow time (72.0 s) but 7200 vph capacity, so its BPR cost stays ≈ free-flow regardless of load over the demand range here. The free-flow (selfish) `naive` router routes EVERY request onto the cheaper-at-zero-load edge 0, overloading it (v/c = 2 at 1800 vph) so its realized BPR cost blows up to 36·(1+0.15·2^4) = 122.4 s; a system-optimal split internalizes that congestion externality and moves ~half the demand to edge 1, cutting the realized total network time roughly in half. Hand math at D = 1800 vph: naive realized total ≈ 220320; optimal split (xA ≈ 967, xB ≈ 833) ≈ 101749; PoA ≈ 2.17. The benchmark's PoA(naive) is therefore comfortably > 1, and systemoptimal's realized total ≤ naive's, which the toy network cannot demonstrate (see engine/internal/routing/systemoptimal_test.go TestSystemOptimalNoWorseThanUE, which defers this strict-PoA fixture to Phase 4). All values computed at capacity_scale=1.0 via the §2 derivation rules exactly (capacity_vph = lanes × 1800 × class_factor; freeflow_time_s = length_m / (maxspeed_kmh / 3.6)). osm_way_ids are fresh 91000xx ids, disjoint from toy_network.geojson, toy_network_adversarial.geojson, and the congestion fixture, so no fixture ever collides. Region: NYC-ish, lon [-73.97..-73.965], lat [40.74..40.743]. Both edges share endpoint nodes 0 and 1; their length_m (600 m) is ≥ the ~537 m great-circle endpoint chord, satisfying the #81/#87 loader guard. Edge 1 carries an interior geometry shape point so the two parallel edges have distinct LineStrings; the shape point is NOT a graph node (NodeCount counts only the 2 endpoints) and does not affect the endpoint chord. See README.md.

features.note: CHEAP, LOW-CAPACITY Pigou link: one-way node0(origin)->node1, the lower free-flow time (36.0 s) so the free-flow `naive` router selects it for EVERY request, but only 900 vph capacity so it congests sharply under load (v/c=2 at 1800 vph ⇒ realized BPR cost 36·(1+0.15·2^4)=122.4 s). class residential ⇒ class_factor 0.5; capacity=1*1800*0.5=900; freeflow=600/(60/3.6)=36.0; length_m 600 ≥ ~537 m endpoint chord.

NEAR-CONSTANT, HIGH-CAPACITY Pigou link: one-way node0(origin)->node1 PARALLEL to edge 0 (same endpoint nodes, distinct LineString via an interior shape point that is NOT a graph node). Higher free-flow time (72.0 s) so `naive` never picks it at zero load, but 7200 vph capacity keeps its realized BPR cost ≈ 72 s across the demand range (v/c=0.25 at 1800 vph ⇒ cost 72·(1+0.15·0.25^4)≈72.04 s). A system-optimal split moves ~half the demand here, internalizing edge 0's congestion externality. class motorway ⇒ class_factor 1.0; capacity=4*1800*1.0=7200; freeflow=600/(30/3.6)=72.0; length_m 600 ≥ ~537 m endpoint chord.
